question: My home internet contract has an early cancellation fee. What minimum trial period does the CRTC Internet Code give me if my provider is covered?
generated_answer:
The CRTC Internet Code requires that providers give a minimum 30-day trial period for new customers. However, if your contract has an early cancellation fee, the provider may offer a longer trial period to offset this fee. You should check your contract or contact your provider to confirm the specific trial period they offer.

If you're not satisfied with the service during the trial period and want to cancel, you'll need to pay the early cancellation fee. But if you cancel within the trial period, you shouldn't have to pay the full fee. The provider should clearly explain the terms of the trial period and any associated fees when you sign up.

It's also worth noting that the CRTC Internet Code requires providers to give customers a 15-day notice period before increasing prices or changing terms of the contract. This gives you time to decide whether to stay with the provider or switch to another one.

If you're unsure about your rights or the terms of your contract, you can contact the CRTC or your provider's customer service for clarification. They can help you understand your options and ensure you're treated fairly under the CRTC Internet Code.
